workflows.name: Make-to-order metal fabrication
workflows.desc: Custom and engineered-to-order steel, sheet metal and structural work: quoting from drawings, job routings, outside processing and job costing.

caps.d: Build quotes from drawings with material, labour and outside-processing costs, then convert to a job.
Rules-based configurator (CPQ) that generates the BOM and routing for a custom order.
Multi-level, job-specific BOMs and routings that can be changed per order.
Send parts out for galvanizing, painting or machining and track them as a routing step.
Integration with nesting software and CAD, including plate and sheet remnants.
Tablet or kiosk clock-in to jobs and operations, with real-time job status.
Capacity-based scheduling of work centres instead of a whiteboard.
Estimated versus actual cost per job, by material, labour and burden.

workflows.name: Coil and sheet processing
workflows.desc: Metals service centres and roll-formers that buy by weight and sell by length or piece: slitting, cut-to-length, traceability and tolling.

caps.d: Stock, buy and sell the same item in weight, length and pieces (lb, kg, ft, m, sheets) without manual conversion.
Track each coil and heat number from receipt to shipment, with mill test certificates attached.
Processing orders that turn one master coil into several outputs, with yield and scrap recorded.
Process customer-owned material and invoice the service only.
Put usable remnants back into stock with their real dimensions and value.
Read weights from floor scales straight into receiving and production.
Calculate theoretical weight from gauge, width and length, and reconcile with scale weight.
Print coil, bundle and skid tags with barcodes and traceability data.

workflows.name: Batch chemical and process
workflows.desc: Chemicals, coatings, adhesives, food ingredients and other formula-based producers: recipes, lots, potency, QC and compliance.

caps.d: Recipe management with versioning and scaling to batch size.
Forward and backward traceability of every raw-material lot into finished lots.
Adjust formulas for active-ingredient strength and handle variable weights.
Quality holds, test results and certificates of analysis (COA) per lot.
Safety data sheets, hazard labels and regulatory documents tied to products.
One batch producing several outputs, with costs split between them.
Expiry and retest dates, with first-expired-first-out (FEFO) allocation.
Actual batch cost including yield loss, rework and overhead.

workflows.name: Warehouse management (WMS)
workflows.desc: Distributors, e-commerce sellers and manufacturers with their own warehouse: locations, scanning, picking, counting and shipping.

caps.d: Stock held by bin and location, not just by warehouse.
Handheld or phone scanning for receiving, moves, picking and counting.
System tells staff where to put stock, using slotting rules and cross-docking.
Batch, zone and wave picking with optimised pick paths.
Scheduled cycle counts by ABC class or location, with variance approval.
Lot and serial tracking with FEFO picking.
Packing, cartonization, carrier rate shopping and label printing.
Connectors for Shopify, Amazon and EDI (850, 856 ASN, 810).

rc.cost: Licences are only part of it: plan for a services budget of at least the first-year subscription.
rc.uom: Weight-to-length conversions work but need careful set-up of UOM classes before go-live.
rc.floor: Strong shop-floor module; success depends on tablet placement and supervisor discipline.
rc.hidden: Advanced scheduling, configurator and advanced warehouse modules are separate line items.

rc.cost: Usually sold as an all-in-one suite, so fewer add-on surprises than modular platforms.
rc.uom: Handles purchase-by-weight, issue-by-length; test your actual plate and bar items in the demo.
rc.floor: Built for the shop floor; operators adapt quickly if data collection is kept to a few taps.
rc.hidden: Report customisation and data migration of open jobs take longer than planned.

rc.cost: Predictable subscription; budget separately for training time on the floor.
rc.uom: Fine for job-shop materials; not designed for coil processing.
rc.floor: Simple job clock-in works well on shared kiosks.
rc.hidden: Check payroll and Canadian tax handling through the accounting link you plan to use.

vendors.name: ProShop ERP
vendors.best: Precision machining and regulated job shops

rc.cost: Includes quality management, which can replace a separate QMS subscription.
rc.uom: Not intended for weight-based coil or bulk inventory.
rc.floor: Paperless shop-floor approach; needs screens at most work centres.
rc.hidden: The paperless approach needs time to digitise work instructions and inspection plans.

rc.cost: Strong configurator, but configuration rules need an experienced partner to build.
rc.uom: Flexible UOM; define conversions per item early.
rc.floor: Shop-floor and warehouse scanning are usually added through a companion module.
rc.hidden: Partner quality varies; ask for references in your own industry.

rc.cost: Low entry price; the real cost is in the add-ons (ISV apps) needed for niche manufacturing.
rc.uom: Item UOMs are basic; coil and potency logic usually come from a partner app.
rc.floor: Native shop-floor tools are light; most manufacturers add an MES or data-collection app.
rc.hidden: Each ISV app adds its own subscription and upgrade dependency.

vendors.name: Acumatica Manufacturing Edition
vendors.best: SMEs wanting cloud ERP with manufacturing and distribution

rc.cost: Priced by resources, not users, which suits shops with many occasional users.
rc.uom: Standard UOM conversions; heavy weight/length logic needs testing.
rc.floor: Mobile app supports warehouse scanning well; shop-floor data collection is adequate.
rc.hidden: Advanced planning and estimating are separate modules within the edition.

rc.cost: Renewal increases are a common surprise; negotiate a price cap in the first contract.
rc.uom: Fine for distribution UOMs; coil and formula logic needs third-party apps.
rc.floor: WMS mobile is strong; shop-floor manufacturing is lighter than specialist ERPs.
rc.hidden: Advanced manufacturing, WMS and planning are add-on modules.

vendors.name: SAP Business One
vendors.best: SMEs that want SAP with partner add-ons

rc.cost: Core is affordable; manufacturing depth usually depends on a partner add-on.
rc.uom: Basic UOM groups; potency and catch weight come from add-ons.
rc.floor: Shop-floor readiness depends entirely on the add-on chosen.
rc.hidden: You are buying the partner as much as the product; check their manufacturing references.

rc.cost: Mature and stable; budget for a solid partner-led implementation.
rc.uom: Handles alternate UOMs and lot traceability well.
rc.floor: Warehouse scanning available; shop-floor capture needs set-up per work centre.
rc.hidden: Customisations can complicate upgrades; keep them to a minimum.

vendors.name: Invera stratixERP
vendors.best: Metals service centres and coil processors

rc.cost: Built for metals, so less customisation, but implementation is still a major project.
rc.uom: Weight, length and piece handling is the core of the product: the strongest fit for coil.
rc.floor: Processing and warehouse scanning are designed for metals yards.
rc.hidden: Less suited if you also do heavy custom fabrication; check fab routing depth.

vendors.name: Deacom (ECI)
vendors.best: Batch process manufacturers: chemicals, coatings, food

rc.cost: Single-database design limits add-on costs; implementation still needs a dedicated internal lead.
rc.uom: Strong for formula units (kg, L, gallons) and catch weight.
rc.floor: Batch tickets and lot capture work well on tablets in the plant.
rc.hidden: Check that SDS authoring for Canada (WHMIS 2015) is included or needs a third party.

rc.cost: Often paired with an accounting platform; confirm which one and who supports the link.
rc.uom: Formula and potency handling is the product's strength.
rc.floor: Plant floor use depends on the scanning set-up chosen.
rc.hidden: Two-product architecture means two upgrade cycles to manage.

rc.cost: Deep regulatory functions; size the project for validation and documentation work.
rc.uom: Handles potency, catch weight and multi-UOM formulas natively.
rc.floor: Plant data capture available; plan device and network coverage early.
rc.hidden: Aptean has several process ERPs; confirm which product and roadmap you are buying.

rc.cost: A big step up from Sage 50 or 300; do not assume a simple upgrade path.
rc.uom: Good lot, expiry and multi-UOM handling.
rc.floor: Warehouse scanning through a partner solution is common.
rc.hidden: Partner capacity in Canada is uneven; check who will support you after go-live.

rc.cost: Low licence cost; quality of the implementation partner decides the outcome.
rc.uom: UOM categories work for simple cases; weight-per-length logic needs custom code.
rc.floor: Barcode app works well for warehouse; shop-floor tablets need careful set-up.
rc.hidden: Custom modules can break on version upgrades; keep a list of every customisation.

rc.cost: Fast and affordable; expect to outgrow it once you need job costing or detailed routings.
rc.uom: Simple UOMs only.
rc.floor: Shop-floor app is easy for small teams.
rc.hidden: Accounting stays in QuickBooks or Xero, so check the sync for Canadian tax.

rc.cost: Low monthly cost per user; a good first system for 5–30 staff.
rc.uom: Basic UOM conversions.
rc.floor: Simple production reporting works on tablets.
rc.hidden: Limited for multi-site or complex job shops; plan your next step.

vendors.name: Fishbowl
vendors.best: QuickBooks users needing inventory and light manufacturing

rc.cost: Extends QuickBooks rather than replacing it.
rc.uom: Simple UOM conversions.
rc.floor: Barcode scanning for warehouse is the main strength.
rc.hidden: Check how well it works with QuickBooks Online Canada versus Desktop.

rc.cost: Priced for order volume; model your peak season, not your average month.
rc.uom: Each, case and pallet handling is standard.
rc.floor: Designed for mobile-first warehouse teams.
rc.hidden: You still need an ERP or accounting system; budget for the integration.

rc.cost: Mid-market WMS depth; above SME budgets for very small warehouses.
rc.uom: Full pack-level UOM and lot handling.
rc.floor: Strong mobile workflows and labour tracking.
rc.hidden: ERP integration scope is the main cost driver; define it up front.

rc.cost: Built around 3PL billing; less suited to a manufacturer's own warehouse.
rc.uom: Handles client-specific UOMs.
rc.floor: Mobile scanning is standard.
rc.hidden: Each client connection (EDI, marketplace) can carry its own fee.

rc.cost: Strongest value when bought with racking or automation projects.
rc.uom: Full pack-level and lot handling.
rc.floor: Good RF workflows; automation interfaces included.
rc.hidden: Integration with SME ERPs may need custom connector work.
